reasoning:
The CODE READING is correct and I re-verified every leg of it independently: value-history.js:100 returns `baseline.rank - latest.rank`, so a positive trend7 IS a rise; server.py:3354 movers docstring 'Risers = rank improved (number got smaller)'; MoversPanel.jsx:198 heads risers 'sell-high candidates'; signal-engine.js:151-160 and its Python mirror src/api/terminal.py:970-976 both emit BUY for trend7 >= +3 with non-high volatility. Two opposite verbs off the same rank-history sign. That part survives.

What does not survive is the finding's framing of the evidence and its blast radius.

(1) NOT OBSERVED AT RUNTIME. `data/rank_history.jsonl` does not exist in this container. /api/movers returns historyDepthDays:0, risers:[], fallers:[]; /api/terminal returns signals:[]; the page renders 'No qualifying movers in this window' under BOTH headings and 'Buy 0'. Every trend7 is null, so `(c.trend7 ?? 0) >= 3` is false and buy.uptrend_controlled cannot fire. The reproduction command proves only that two HEADINGS co-exist on one page — it does not, and in this container cannot, exhibit one player carrying both labels. numericProof is therefore a code reading dressed as a measurement. In production (where the scrape appends rank history) the collision would be reachable, so this is not overturned — but the finding's confidence:high is not earned by what was actually run.

(2) pagesAffected 2 is wrong. '/trending' does not render MoversPanel and contains no sell-high framing — it computes its own movers from contract rows via lib computeMovers. MoversPanel.jsx:198 is the only 'sell-high candidates' string in the tree and TerminalLayout.jsx:76 is its only mount. pagesAffected = 1 (/).

(3) playersAffected 1072 is wrong by two orders of magnitude. /api/movers caps at limit=10 per side (server.py, `limit = max(1, min(50, limit))`, default 10) and the Signals panel is roster-scoped ('per roster player'). The observable collision set is bounded by 10 risers intersected with a ~30-player roster, not the 1,072-row board.

(4) The collision is narrower than 'any rise'. STRONG_HOLD (priority 50, signal-engine.js:131-147 / terminal.py:963-969) outranks BUY (priority 40). A riser with value >= 7000 and trend30 >= 0 returns STRONG_HOLD, not BUY. The BUY-vs-sell-high contradiction is confined to sub-7000 risers, or elite risers whose 30d trend is negative.

(5) The finding UNDERCOUNTS the theses. A third momentum consumer on the same page uses the reversal thesis: frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:556 feeds ScoutingIntel on / with 'Down N ranks in 7d ... potential buy-low if league treats it the same.' So it is 2 reversal panels vs 1 following panel, and signal-engine is the outlier — which sharpens 'which one should change' but does not add a fourth interpretation.

Severity: P1 overstates it. This is not a wrong number a user acts on — it is inconsistent prescriptive framing between two unvalidated heuristics measured over DIFFERENT windows and thresholds (movers: 14d default, threshold 15; signal: 7d, threshold 3), and it renders nowhere today. Real, worth fixing, P2.

whatWouldSettleIt: A populated data/rank_history.jsonl (>= 7 days deep) plus a selected team, then one query listing players that appear in /api/movers risers AND carry signal==BUY with tag uptrend_controlled in /api/terminal signals for the same roster. A non-empty intersection settles it as a live user-facing contradiction; an empty one after several scrapes would mean the 14d/threshold-15 and 7d/threshold-3 windows never actually overlap in practice and the finding collapses to a copy inconsistency.

reasoning:
UPHELD ON SUBSTANCE, rescoped on mechanism and blast radius. The reproduction runs today and returns the stated number exactly — 21/51 legs (41.2%) at the unadjusted value under valuationMode:leagueAdjusted — and I reproduced the mechanism per-leg rather than trusting the aggregate. The numericProof checks out to the digit: Kenneth Walker rdv 5813, factor 1.041554, round(5813*1.041554)=6055, served 5831 = offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue. src/league_intel/overlay.py:86-93 scales exactly one key (copy['rankDerivedValue']) and offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue rides through untouched; the response stamps leagueAdjusted with valuationNote:null, so nothing on screen says otherwise. The client-side inconsistency is real too — dynasty-data.js:1943-1952 additionally scales values.overall/finalAdjusted/displayValue and :1978 _finalAdjusted, and neither side touches the offense-only key. The lens toggle is live and user-reachable (frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1656).

RESCOPED BROADER on mechanism. The finding frames this as a SERIALIZATION defect (suggestions.py:1737-1741, displayValue). It is not — it is an ARITHMETIC defect. `_eff_val(p, offense_only)` (suggestions.py:760-768) is called at :1038, :1044-1045, :1049, :1052-1053, :1091, :1099, :1111-1112, :1177-1203, :1253, :1258 — it is what picks the trade targets, sets give_val/recv_val, and drives gap and fairness. So under the adjusted lens an IDP-free suggestion is CONSTRUCTED on the unadjusted board, not merely labelled with unadjusted numbers. Fixing the serializer alone would leave wrong trades with right-looking prices.

RESCOPED BROADER on routes. The finding names 2 routes and claims routesAffected:6 without recounting. I measured a third route failing the same way: /api/trade/simulate returns a byte-identical delta (totalValue 1754, KW at 5831) under market and leagueAdjusted for an IDP-free trade, via src/api/trade_simulator.py:63-64 reading offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue. The control case proves the route is otherwise wired correctly (5813 -> 6055 with an IDP leg present), so this is the same offense-only hole, not a separate defect. src/trade/finder.py:248-249 substitutes offense_only_model_value (mirrored from _offenseOnlyFinalAdjusted, finder.py:479) on the same condition and is affected identically. Three engine routes materially, not 2 and not 6.

RESCOPED NARROWER on players. 606 is the count of rows CARRYING an offense-only value. Only 416 of those also carry a league factor, so only 416 could have moved under the lens; for the other 190 the market and adjusted answers are identical anyway and there is nothing to be wrong about.

Severity stays P1, deliberately not P0. The served number is a real market value, not a fabricated one, and the factors measured here span roughly 1.01-1.10, so the error is low single-digit percent — on a lens the repo's own backtest (docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md) records as 'no difference detected'. A user is misled about WHICH board they are on, not handed a nonsense price.

reasoning:
The arithmetic is right and I reproduced it three times. sideAMean 9437-9447 against a board value of 9947, and the finding's analytic derivation lands on 9442.98 — inside its own 25-point tolerance. I also ran the control the finding did not: with an unclamped value the sampled mean equals the board value to 0.008% (8000.6 vs 8000), which PROVES the extended-triangular quantile map (monte_carlo.py:104-131) is mean-preserving and that max(0, min(9999, v)) in _shifted (monte_carlo.py:365-366) is the sole cause. The 0-of-1092-valueBand count reproduces exactly. The flag is default-ON (feature_flags.py:112), so the route is live and /trade reaches it.

Two corrections, one of which is a wrong code path.

(1) THE CITED LIVE PATH IS WRONG. codeRefs point at monte_carlo.py:368-387 and the observed text says 'the fallback IS the production path for every asset'. It is not the production path for /trade. MonteCarloButton.jsx:41-60 ALWAYS attaches an explicit valueBand to every asset it posts — it synthesizes p10=v*0.85, p50=v, p90=v*1.15 itself and rounds them — so the backend takes the valueBand branch at monte_carlo.py:368-376, never the fallback at :379-387. The finding's substance is untouched (the client fabricates the numerically identical band, and _shifted clamps p90 in BOTH branches, so the 9999 bias bites on the real page too), but the fallback branch is reached only by direct API callers, and a repair aimed only at monte_carlo.py's fallback would not change what /trade does.

(2) BLAST RADIUS CONFLATES TWO CLAIMS. playersAffected:1092 is honest for the fabricated-±15%-band half (0 of 1092 rows carry a valueBand — verified). It is wrong for the 9999-clamp half, which is what the title leads with and what the numericProof measures. Exactly 12 of 1092 rows satisfy rankDerivedValue*1.15 > 9999, and the bias across them is not a flat 5.07% — it is bias = 0.35*min(9999, 1.15v) - 0.4025v, running from -5.21% (Josh Allen) down to -0.27% (Caleb Williams). Only 6 of the 12 exceed 2%. '5.07%' is the Bowers case, near the worst case, not a population figure.

One thing that STRENGTHENS the finding and the author missed: server.py:11358-11360 states 'The labelHint + disclaimer fields are PART OF THE CONTRACT — the frontend MUST render the disclaimer somewhere visible so users don't mis-read win probability as real-world odds.' grep for 'disclaimer' in MonteCarloButton.jsx returns nothing, and the component's own header docstring says the output is rewritten in plain English with no 'consensus-band samples' language. So the mandated warning is not rendered. That is the closest this comes to P0 territory.

Severity: P1 held. The self-assigned P1 is defensible and I am not escalating it: the fabricated band is uninformative rather than fabricated-in-a-direction for 1,080 of 1,092 rows, and the directional bias the title leads with touches 12 elite assets. The 'no warning shown' condition IS met, but the mispricing is 0.3-5% on a dozen players, not an order-of-magnitude error.
